# A range mark whose own content carries another mark

An index mark with no `entry=` indexes under its visible text, and a mark may
sit inside another mark's content. The two are unremarkable apart; together
they are the shape this fixture exists for. The emitting pass rewrites the
inner mark before it reaches the outer one, so the outer mark's visible text
is not the same object in the two passes that read it — and the range verdict
the outer mark takes must not depend on that.

Both ends of this range carry the nested shape, so the outer entry is one term
in both passes or in neither.

The discussion of [nixie [ogopogo]{.index}]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

# A plain range of another term, opening inside the nested one

The untouched shape: a range written with no nesting anywhere near it. It
opens and closes inside the nested range above, so the two ranges overlap and
a verdict handed to the wrong mark would show as a span of the wrong width
rather than as a missing entry.

The discussion of [pooka]{.index range="open"} begins here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [pooka]{.index range="close"} ends here.

{{< pagebreak >}}

And the discussion of [nixie [ogopogo]{.index}]{.index range="close"} ends
here.
